question: Does the reusable 2015 Palawan Stiphodon paper support additional named-site observations and a narrowly described natural-feeding behavior?

source.title: A new species of the genus Stiphodon from Palawan, Philippines (Gobiidae: Sicydiinae)
source.citation: Maeda, K. & Palla, H. P. (2015). A new species of the genus Stiphodon from Palawan, Philippines (Gobiidae: Sicydiinae). Zootaxa, 4018(3), 381–395. https://doi.org/10.11646/zootaxa.4018.3.3.
source.licenseEvidence: The publisher PDF states on its first page that the article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution License and links CC BY 3.0.

names.name: Stiphodon percnopterygionus
names.status: Valid as Stiphodon percnopterygionus Watson & Chen 1998

taxonomyCrosscheck.limitation: The Catalog supports nomenclatural status only; it does not independently re-identify the paper's collected specimen or field observations.

extraction.method: Reviewed the publisher-hosted full article. Transcribed only named locality, source date, source-stated specimen or field-observation context, voucher details, and the explicitly observed feeding behavior. No source prose, figure, photo, map, coordinates, or geometry was copied.

additionalSpeciesObservations.locality: Balsahan Stream in the Iwahig Prison and Penal Farm, Puerto Princesa City, Palawan
additionalSpeciesObservations.reportedEvidence: Three female individuals were found. Two of the three were collected and listed as comparative material. The figure caption identifies one collected female as WPU-PPC-P 10, 43.7 mm standard length.
additionalSpeciesObservations.evidenceKind: field observation with partial voucher detail
additionalSpeciesObservations.countMeaning: Three source-reported individuals found; two collected; no standardized population count or abundance estimate.

additionalSpeciesObservations.locality: Balsahan Stream in the Iwahig Prison and Penal Farm, Puerto Princesa City, Palawan
additionalSpeciesObservations.reportedEvidence: One wild male was identified on site by snorkel observation from body and fin markings. The article explicitly says it was not collected and lists no voucher.
additionalSpeciesObservations.evidenceKind: direct field observation; no specimen collected
additionalSpeciesObservations.countMeaning: One observed individual is a source observation, not an abundance estimate.

additionalSpeciesObservations.locality: Iwahig River, Puerto Princesa City, Palawan
additionalSpeciesObservations.reportedEvidence: One preserved specimen, NSMT-P 45093, 51.2 mm standard length.

additionalSpeciesObservations.locality: Iwahig River at Quezon, Palawan, South China Sea side; distinct from Iwahig River at Puerto Princesa City
additionalSpeciesObservations.reportedEvidence: The authors describe the species as abundant during a two-day exploration, without a numeric count or voucher for this field observation.
additionalSpeciesObservations.evidenceKind: field observation; no voucher or numeric count reported
additionalSpeciesObservations.countMeaning: The source's qualitative term is retained as context only and is not converted to a number.

localities: Middle reaches of Balsahan Stream, Puerto Princesa City
Middle reaches of Barake Stream, Aborlan
naturalFeedingObservation.reportedEvidence: The authors observed fish clinging to rocks while feeding on algae.
naturalFeedingObservation.limits: This is not a gut-content analysis, quantified diet, complete diet, current-presence record, or bait recommendation.

projectionDecision.feedingEvidenceType: directly observed feeding behavior, not gut contents
projectionDecision.scopeSpecificReuse: A second, separately scoped attributed projection under CC BY 3.0: paraphrased named-site observation and voucher facts for three additional Stiphodon species, plus one named-site observation of Stiphodon palawanensis feeding on algae. No article text, images, figures, coordinates, or geometry are reproduced. This is not blanket approval for other article content.

caveats: The 2015 observations and 1988 voucher are historical evidence, not current-presence or standardized abundance estimates.
A named field observation without a collected voucher remains distinct from a preserved specimen record.
The two Iwahig River localities are separate: one is at Puerto Princesa City on the Sulu Sea side; the other is at Quezon on the South China Sea side. No geometry or channel connection is inferred.
The qualitative word abundant is not converted into a numeric count.
The algae entry represents directly observed feeding behavior at two study sites, not stomach-content composition, a complete diet, or bait effectiveness.
Current Catalog of Fishes statuses support names only and do not independently re-identify source observations or confirm present-day occurrence.
The source reports a geographically limited exploration and calls for comprehensive surveys; these records do not complete Palawan or MIMAROPA coverage.

followUp.nextAction: Continue source discovery for Palawan lake, river, stream, wetland, brackish and coastal fish; preserve locality, voucher, taxonomy, effort and rights distinctions. This paper is a narrow freshwater source, not a regional checklist.
